incentives.title: Incentives
incentives.standardClass: Standard tax class: no class incentive applies.
incentives.classIncentive: This lot's tax class carries an incentive (see details).

define.tax: The yearly property tax bill, as the County computes it for the latest bill year. A new owner's bill can differ once exemptions drop or the lot is reassessed.
define.value: What the Cook County Assessor says the property is worth: its assessed value divided by the share the law assesses for its class. It sets the tax bill; it is not a sale price.
define.sales: Recorded sales of similar properties near this lot (same tax class), counted only when the County treats them as market sales. The chips say how near and how recent.
define.rent: What renters nearby pay each month, rent plus utilities, from the Census survey of this tract (or a wider area). Not listing prices, and not what a new building would get.
define.incentives: Programs that can help pay for a project in this place: tax-increment money, tax credits and zones with tax breaks. Being inside one means a project can apply, not that it is approved.

program.tif: Tax Increment Financing: a district where growth in property tax pays for public projects and can help private development.
program.oz: A federal Opportunity Zone: investors can defer or cut capital-gains tax by investing here.
program.ez: A State of Illinois Enterprise Zone: sales-tax and other breaks for building and businesses.
program.qct: A HUD Qualified Census Tract: affordable-housing projects here can get a larger federal tax credit.
program.nmtc: A tract eligible for New Markets Tax Credits, a federal credit for investment in low-income areas.
